item.title: Where Private Investigation Firms and Claims Professionals Intersect
item.description: The most effective private investigation firms intentionally build teams that understand both sides of the claims process. View Series Prior to joining the private investigation industry, I spent nine years working in insurance claims handling and Special Investigations Unit (SIU) roles. Although claims professionals and private investigators work for different organizations, we ultimately share the same objective.

item.title: The Takeaway: Go to Where the Problem Lives
item.description: The trucking project described in the accompanying article, “ Design the Team Before You Design the Solution: Commercial Trucking Case Study ,” succeeded when a team shifted its perspective on whose problem it was solving. Here’s how to build the learnings captured by the case study into how you and your team approach your next complex problem. Before bringing in outside perspectives, write down your current working theory of the problem.

item.title: Design the Team Before You Design the Solution: Commercial Trucking Case Study
item.description: Below the article, Bassett summarizes takeaways from the case study, providing a How-To guide to help readers design the teams they need to solve their next complex problems. For readers interested in a tear sheet, the takeaways are also published separately in the linked article, " Go to Where the Problem Lives ." Carrier Management previously published an article about how to address the problem of strategic drift that can stall innovation teams, " Reframing Like a Fox: How Insurance Leaders Can Catch Strategic Drift Before It Compounds ." In this article, we explore an insurance case study that illustrates how understanding the way that we individually interpret a problem—shaped by how we perceive our environment—is key to assembling teams that can see a challenge both in its parts and as a whole. One topic that we returned to repeatedly was small commercial trucking fleets—logistics firms with fewer than 16 cabs that had often grown from owner-operator arrangements into complex businesses that required real management oversight.

item.title: Tribunal upholds FCA ban on pair involved in pension transfer advice and reduces fines
item.description: The Tribunal found that Ms Dunne falsely claimed she had given advice to some pension schemes before she had done so. Also, that she had failed to take proper care when giving pension transfer advice. The Tribunal ruled that the fines should reflect its finding that 18% of Ms Dunne's clients received unsuitable advice.

item.title: A Record 14 Billion-Dollar Rounds In July Pushed Venture’s Historic Run Higher
item.description: Startup capital totaled $65 billion, up 100% year over year, as the month notched the highest-ever number of billion-dollar venture rounds on record, per Crunchbase data. Fourteen startups raised billion-dollar rounds in July, the highest count in a single month, though not the largest amount raised in such deals, an analysis of Crunchbase data shows. July ranked as the third-largest funding month of the year, up 10% over June, following on the heels of a record-breaking first half of 2026 , when startups raised $515 billion globally.

item.title: TWIA renewal came in almost 12% under budget. Staff to recommend Gallagher Re continue
item.description: The Texas Windstorm Insurance Association’s (TWIA) reinsurance and catastrophe bond renewal for 2026 came in almost 12% under its budgeted spend for the coverage, while at a meeting later today its staff will recommend it continues with Gallagher Re as its reinsurance broker. The net cost of TWIA’s 2026 reinsurance program came out at $199.4 million, which is almost 12% under the budgeted amount of $225.2 million. TWIA’s staff will explain that, “The favorable budget variance is a result of the PML being set slightly below the initial estimate incorporated into the budget as well as a softening of the global reinsurance market, resulting in lower reinsurance costs overall.” On a rate-on-line (ROL) basis, it seems TWIA’s program came in around 10% down on the prior year, with an overall ROL for the 2026 reinsurance tower of 9.21%, compared to 10.2% a year earlier.

item.title: Aon promotes Murray to Global Chief Commercial Officer, Captive & Insurance Management
item.description: Aon has promoted long-standing Bermuda based employee Choisel Murray to a senior position as Global Chief Commercial Officer within the Aon Captive & Insurance Management business. Prior to her recent promotion to Global Chief Commercial Officer, Murray was a Deputy Managing Director in Aon’s Captive & Insurance Management division, also with responsibilities in Commercial Risk Solutions. As a result, with insurance management activities sitting within this business unit of the global insurance and reinsurance broker, as well as the captive commercial leadership, Murray will also be the global commercial leader on activities across special purpose insurer (SPI), segregated and protected account structures, which are often utilised to facilitate insurance-linked securities (ILS) arrangements, transform risks to transfer them to the capital markets, and can be issuance vehicles for ILS instruments including catastrophe bonds.

item.title: Talcott launches West Grove Re life and annuity sidecar with $1bn capital raise
item.description: International life and annuity insurance specialist Talcott Financial Group (Talcott) has announced the launch of West Grove Re Ltd., a Bermuda based reinsurance sidecar structure that has been capitalised with approximately $1 billion after a fund-raise in partnership with Goldman Sachs. The roughly $1 billion capital raise for West Grove Re includes equity commitments from Talcott, Goldman Sachs Asset & Wealth Management (AWM) and its clients, as well as a credit facility, Talcott further explained. Talcott becomes the latest major life and annuity player to launch a reinsurance sidecar, to bring third-party capital to support its business.

item.title: Ceres supports California proposal on long-term insurance solvency planning
item.description: In a comment letter submitted to the California Department of Insurance, Ceres said the proposed Long-Term Solvency Planning Regulation would strengthen oversight of the state’s insurance sector while bringing it into line with solvency and transition-planning approaches already adopted by regulators in other parts of the world. Ceres, a US-based non-profit organisation that works with investors, companies and policymakers to advance sustainable business practices and improve the management of climate-related financial risks, has voiced its support for a proposed California regulation that would require the state’s largest domestic insurers to prepare long-term solvency plans addressing financial risks, including those linked to extreme weather. Commenting on the proposal, Steven Rothstein, Chief Programme Officer at Ceres, said the regulation would provide “much needed visibility into how carriers are preparing for future risk.” He added that California’s residents, communities and businesses needed “an insurance market capable of weathering the climate and technology challenges ahead,” describing the proposed framework as an important step towards building that resilience.

item.title: Lockton expands availability of AI-enabled intelligence platform across US business
item.description: Lockton, a privately held insurance brokerage and risk management firm, has announced that its Lockton SAGE enterprise intelligence platform is now being made available more widely across its US business. The platform has been developed to combine Lockton’s proprietary data, advanced analytics, AI-enabled technology and specialist knowledge to help clients make more informed decisions. Originally launched within Lockton Re, Lockton SAGE is now being expanded across Lockton’s wider US operations, including Risk Solutions, People Solutions and Reinsurance, according to the firm.

item.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani’s Rent Freeze Heaps Pressure on a Teetering CMBS Deal
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s rent freeze threatens to make it worse. The deal has become a closely watched barometer of the investability of rent-stabilized housing sectors in New York and, increasingly, nationwide as more cities tighten or consider rent controls . Market watchers say the looming freeze — a central promise of Mamdani’s campaign that launched him into City Hall — will further erode recoveries and discourage capital from flowing into the sector.

item.title: Washington Man Charged With Starting Devastating Spokane Fire
item.description: A 37-year-old Washington State man has been arrested and charged with arson in connection with one of the wildfires that is devastating Spokane, the County Sheriff’s Office said in a statement. Related: Wildfires Destroy Hundreds of Structures in Washington State Farinacci was charged with first-degree arson in connection with the Old Trails Fire, which has destroyed hundred of homes, officials said. The three major fires surrounding Spokane have burned more than 8,000 acres (3,237 hectares) as of Monday morning and have not been contained, according to InciWeb, a federal fire tracking website.

item.title: Oxbow Partners launches CEO Agenda for AI in commercial and specialty (re)insurance
item.description: It also sets out how CEOs should think about AI as a strategic capability, including where it may change operating models, decision rights, talent requirements and the way specialist insurance businesses compete.  Key findings from the report include:  AI advantage in commercial and specialty reinsurance is likely to compound where it improves judgement on complex risks and portfolios CEOs need to look beyond productivity use cases and decide where AI changes the organisation’s shape, motion and direction Leadership teams should assess whether they have the operating model, governance and data foundations to scale AI responsibly The firms that move fastest may not be those with the most pilots, but those that make AI part of how strategic and underwriting decisions are made The post Oxbow Partners launches CEO Agenda for AI in commercial and specialty (re)insurance appeared first on Insurtech Insights . The report, The Oxbow Partners AI CEO Agenda: Compounding advantage with AI in commercial and specialty (re)insurance, sets out how CEOs should move beyond experimentation and build the operating model, governance and decision-making capabilities needed to turn AI investment into competitive advantage. Oxbow Partners has published a new CEO Agenda report arguing that AI will only create lasting advantage in commercial and specialty reinsurance when it helps leadership teams make better judgements in complex, high-value markets.

item.title: Orion180 expands private flood insurance to California
item.description: Orion180 Insurance has launched Residential Private Flood Insurance in California, expanding its flood offering beyond the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP). item.title: Wildfires Fan Record Sales of Catastrophe Bonds to Backstop Risk
item.description: Insurers are turning to catastrophe bonds to pass on historic levels of wildfire risk to the capital markets. Related: Wildfires Destroy Hundreds of Structures in Washington State Catastrophe bonds are designed to help insurers offload unmanageable risks to the capital markets. Issuance of cat bonds that include exposure to wildfires has already soared to more than $5 billion so far this year, according to data published on Monday by industry specialist Artemis.

item.title: TikTok Finalizing Trio of Settlements in Addiction Litigation
item.description: TikTok is finalizing agreements to settle three upcoming trials related to allegations that its video product is addictive and harmful to minors. This trio of cases are part of broad litigation against the world’s largest social media companies, which includes individual plaintiffs alleging harm as well as US school districts and state attorneys general who have made similar claims. Related: Snap Nears Settlement of Addiction Case Ahead of Jury Trial TikTok, Meta Platforms Inc., Google’s YouTube and Snap Inc.’s Snapchat are facing more than 3,000 individual complaints from young users or their families alleging that their products are addictive and have harmed the mental health of children.

item.title: Lockton Re executes ILW covering property cat and cyber risks in a single limit
item.description: Reinsurance broker Lockton Re has successfully executed what the firm believes is the first industry-loss warranty (ILW) that combines property catastrophe and cyber risk triggers within a single limit structure for a protection buying client. Lockton Re explained that this demonstrates how the industry-loss warranty (ILW) market can continued to evolve beyond traditional property-only use-cases, while further underscoring the increasing maturity of the cyber ILW and industry-loss index trigger sector. As the ILW market continues to evolve, we are seeing broader demand from clients for risk solutions that look at new structures and integrated options, and we are particularly excited about the opportunity for growth in this space with more bespoke, alternative index covers for our clients.” Theo Norris, International ILS and Cyber ILS Leader, Lockton Re Capital Markets, further stated, “This deal highlights trends we are seeing with the convergence of property catastrophe and cyber risk transfer, the growing maturity of industry cyber loss indices, and the development of new capital solutions for the market.

item.title: Bowhead Specialty’s H1’26 net income jumps 35% on premium growth and underwriting profitability
item.description: Bowhead Specialty has reported H1 2026 net income of $32.1 million, up 35.3% from $23.8 million in the same period of 2025, as the specialty insurer continued to grow premiums while maintaining an underwriting profit. At the same time, Bowhead’s net investment income rose 40.4% to $36.8 million in H1 2026, and its underwriting profitability remained intact, with the combined ratio improving to 95.6% from 96.9% in H1 2025. In Q2 2026 alone, Bowhead reported net income of $16.1 million, up 30.8% from $12.3 million in H1 2025, while adjusted net income increased 26.5% to $16.1 million.

item.description: According to a new Guy Carpenter report, three major wildfires in Spokane County near Spokane, Washington, have collectively burned 7,000 acres, destroyed more than 700 structures, remain 0% contained, and are expected to continue spreading under favourable conditions, particularly later this week. On Sunday, Spokane County officials reported zero fatalities or injuries due to the fire, while an estimated 60,000 people have been evacuated,” Guy Carpenter observed. Guy Carpenter continued, “Above-normal significant wildfire potential persists across much of the West, with additional hotspots in the southern Plains and Florida during August.

item.title: New Jersey Settles Trucker Misclassification Claims for $2.7 Million
item.description: The New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development (NJDOL) has reached a $2.7 million settlement with STG Logistics, Inc. This settlement resolves the first lawsuit filed under New Jersey’s 2021 law that permits the state to file suit in New Jersey Superior Court against employers who have misclassified workers as independent contractors. STG Logistics purchased XPO’s New Jersey intermodal business in 2022 and assumed liability for the its past employment practices.

item.title: Product-Defect Presumption Lives On: Florida Appeals Court Upholds $103M vs. Ford
item.description: A Florida appeals court has upheld a $103 million jury award against Ford Motor Co. Ford asked the court to set aside or reduce the jury’s 2024 verdict, arguing that the jury should not have been instructed to consider the long-established legal doctrine known as the Cassisi inference, which resulted from a 1981 Florida appeals court decision, Cassisi vs. The appeal was centered on the scope of a Florida legal doctrine that determines when product-defect lawsuits should be heard by a jury.

item.title: UBS Fined $125M by US Regulators for Money Laundering Violations
item.description: In a statement, UBS said it cooperated with regulators and has made significant investments to strengthen its anti-money laundering program “in line with leading industry practices.” Regulators said UBS failed to conduct appropriate due diligence of customers, especially high-risk customers with ties to Russia and Latin America. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) said UBS Financial Services admitted to willfully violating the BSA by failing to implement and maintain an anti-money laundering program and by failing to file suspicious activity reports. One, a Russian oligarch with close ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin, allegedly opened and maintained accounts at UBS despite media reports questioning how he amassed his wealth, and linking him to possible money laundering as well as a company “actively invested” in Iranian digital assets.

item.title: Mapfre to Acquire Stake in Tuio
item.description: (Tuio founders José María Lucas and Juan García y Asís Pardo.) Mapfre (Madrid) has reached an agreement to acquire a 38.9 percent stake in Tuio (Madrid), a Spanish digital insurance distributor. Mapfre says the investment will support Tuio’s expansion beyond Spain into Latin America and Europe, where Mapfre already operates. Tuio was the first insurance app to be integrated within ChatGPT for the sale of insurance products, according to Mapfre.

item.title: SAS, Swiss Re Link Catastrophe Analytics
item.description: (Image source: SAS.) SAS (Cary, N.C.) and Swiss Re (Zurich) have entered into a strategic technology relationship to help insurers incorporate catastrophe risk intelligence into underwriting, pricing and portfolio management workflows. As a member of the SAS Strategic Technology Partner Program, Swiss Re will combine its CatNet natural catastrophe risk intelligence with SAS Insurance Life Cycle Accelerator, according to a SAS statement. “The combination of SAS’ AI and actuarial modeling capabilities with Swiss Re’s catastrophe intelligence will enable insurers to make faster, more transparent and more resilient underwriting and pricing decisions.” The collaboration is aimed partly at so-called secondary perils, including floods, hailstorms and wildfires.

item.title: Guidewire Launches AI Agent Framework
item.description: Kornmesser.) Guidewire (San Mateo, Calif.) has launched Qusar, a new release that introduces an Agentic Framework for building, deploying and managing AI agents on Guidewire Cloud Platform. The framework lets insurers choose the AI model appropriate to a given task and gives agents secure, real-time access to policy, claims and billing data and workflows, according to a Guidewire statement. “Agentic Framework addresses this directly by letting insurers deploy AI within their existing systems and workflows while maintaining operational control and compliance.” Qusar also introduces Guidewire-developed agents for claims and underwriting workflows.

item.title: AI Skills More Valuable Than MBAs, 86% of Finance Executives Say
item.description: financial services executives surveyed by consulting firm PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP say they think AI training is more valuable than an MBA for many new hires, reflecting the urgency companies face in adopting the technology effectively. The survey, released Monday, showed companies are willing to pay accordingly: 91% of executives said they’re increasing compensation for employees with AI skills. and Cloudflare Inc., to ramp up entry-level hiring, betting that recent Gen Z graduates will be able to do more with AI tools than existing employees.

item.title: Hackers Hit Bitcoin’s Safest Hiding Place in Ongoing Attack
item.description: Hackers have found a software flaw in a brand of “cold” Bitcoin wallet — considered one of the safest places to store cryptocurrency — and are siphoning tens of millions of dollars in an ongoing attack. These wallets are supposed to be the safest place to keep cryptocurrency because they are isolated from the internet. notified users of its Coldcard devices that a security flaw in the keys that protect their Bitcoin had compromised some wallets.

item.title: Robotaxis Operating Without Manual Controls, Like Brake Pedals, Coming Soon
item.description: Federal regulators are clearing the way for robotaxis to operate without manual controls like steering wheels or, eventually, even brake pedals as the rules start to catch up to the evolving technology. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration also proposed a rule last month to allow robotaxis to operate without brake pedals, but that proposal is still pending. The Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety Group raised concerns about Zoox’s plan to operate without a steering wheel or other standard controls because the company didn’t provide detailed evidence that showed its vehicles could operate safely on public roads.

item.title: U.S. Safety Agency Says Older Ford Cars, SUVs Pose Unreasonable Safety Risks
item.description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Monday that some older Ford cars and SUVs pose unreasonable safety risks because the timing belt may fail and cause them to lose power or engines to seize. “Based on NHTSA’s analysis of the data, failure rates, information provided by Ford, preliminary engine teardown analysis, and precedent recalls regarding loss of engine oil pressure with the presence of driver-facing warnings, (the agency) believes there is an unreasonable risk to motor vehicle safety,” NHTSA said. auto safety regulator upgraded a defect investigation into about 135,000 Ford Fiesta, Ford Focus and Ford EcoSport vehicles with 1.0L engines from various model years between 2014 and 2021.

item.title: Recreational Vehicle Thefts Decline, But Most Are Never Recovered: NICB
item.description: A new report indicates recreational vehicle thefts have declined by 20 percent, but most are never recovered, according to the National Insurance Crime Bureau. “Although the continued decrease in thefts is encouraging, the fact that nearly two-thirds of stolen recreational vehicles remain unrecovered demonstrates why owners must take proactive steps to protect their property and report a theft as soon as possible.” Motorcycles represented more than three-quarters of all recreational vehicle thefts reported in 2025. More than half of recreational vehicle recoveries occur within two weeks of being reported stolen.

item.title: Saudi Re posts 118% rise in Q2’26 profit
item.description: Riyadh headquartered reinsurance company, Saudi Re, generated net profit after Zakat of SAR 115 million (USD 30.7m) in the second quarter of 2026, a year-on-year increase of a significant 118% from SAR 53 million (USD 14.2m) last year, driven by continued growth across the business. Over the past year, Saudi Re continued to expand across multiple business lines locally and globally, leading to a 71% year-on-year rise in revenues to SAR 1.3 billion (USD 347m) for the first half of 2026. Net profit for the six month period rose 84% year-on-year to SAR 162 million (USD 43.3m), as gross written premiums hit SAR 3.3 billion (USD 882m), an increase of 58% on the prior year’s SAR 2.1 billion (USD 561m).

item.title: Everspan strengthens leadership team, appoints David Kenyon Head of Reinsurance
item.description: “Clay, Bevan and David bring deep expertise in their respective areas, and their addition will strengthen our ability to scale the business while maintaining the underwriting discipline, strong partnerships, and operational focus that are central to our strategy.” Everspan said Kenyon joins with more than 25 years of experience in insurance and reinsurance. Everspan Group, a US specialty property and casualty insurance platform owned by Octave Specialty Group, has appointed three senior executives as the company continues to develop its leadership team in support of its long-term growth strategy. Kenyon joined as Head of Reinsurance on 31 July.
